_note: Primary-source pass on Japan's 30 zero-edge nodes. The highest-yield pattern was each survey's own 'legal basis' (根拠法令) statement citing the Statistics Act No. 53 of 2007 (jp-statistics-act-2007) verbatim, found on stat.go.jp/mext.go.jp/esri.cao.go.jp/enecho.meti.go.jp methodology pages fetched and grep-verified directly (curl required a Referer header to avoid 403s on several meti.go.jp/enecho pages). A second pattern verified MHLW's Vital Statistics cause-of-death coding is explicitly ICD-10-based (who-icd-10), via a PDF extracted with PyPDF2. 10 of 30 nodes (33%) were wired with 10 verified edges; 0 new nodes were needed. The remaining 20 are dropped, roughly half as confirmed no-document (legal basis is a different, non-corpus Act; or citations point to non-corpus sources) and half as deferred behind JS-rendered pages, image-only chart captions with no text citation, or nodes not reached in the time budget (notably the nuclear-regulatory cluster). UPDATE 2026-08-29 (Grok follow-up on the round's blocked-domain leads, raw-verified by the orchestrating session): closed all 3 nuclear-regulatory-cluster leads (reactor status, Fukushima Daiichi decommissioning, spent fuel storage -> jp-nra, all via NRA's own Convention on Nuclear Safety national report PDF) plus e-Stat's own legal basis under the Statistics Act (via an MIC follow-up report PDF, Shift-JIS decoded). Also confirmed jp-long-term-care-insurance's dead end with a verified quote (administrative tally, not survey-derived).

dependencies.basis: Statistics Bureau of Japan's English homepage meta-description states: "The Statistics Bureau and the Director-General for Policy Planning of Japan play the central role in the official statistical system in producing and disseminating basic official statistics, and coordinating statistical work under the Statistics Act and other legislation." This establishes the Statistics Act as SBJ's governing legal framework.

MHLW document on the 2013 partial revision of ICD-10's effect on cause-of-death statistics states (verified via PyPDF2 text extraction): "世界保健機関が勧告する「疾病及び関連保健問題の国際統計分類」（ICD）第10回改訂（ICD-10）の2013年版に準拠した「疾病、傷害及び死因の統計分類」が平成28年に施行（平成27年総務省告示第35号）されたことを受け、人口動態統計では、平成29年より、改正後の分類を死因統計に適用している。" (Translation: Following the 2016 enactment of Japan's 'Statistical Classification of Diseases, Injuries and Causes of Death,' which conforms to the 2013 edition of WHO's ICD-10, Vital Statistics has applied the revised classification to cause-of-death statistics since 2017.) This directly ties Vital Statistics' cause-of-death methodology to ICD-10.

Same MHLW document as above; the detailed cause-of-death and age-specific mortality series within Vital Statistics use the ICD-10-conformant Japanese classification described in: "世界保健機関が勧告する「疾病及び関連保健問題の国際統計分類」（ICD）第10回改訂（ICD-10）の2013年版に準拠した「疾病、傷害及び死因の統計分類」が...人口動態統計では、平成29年より、改正後の分類を死因統計に適用している。" The document's entire body is a table-by-table comparison of old-vs-new ICD-10-based cause-of-death classification counts, which is precisely the detailed cause-specific series this node covers.

METI/Agency for Natural Resources and Energy overview page for the Petroleum Products Supply and Demand Statistics Survey states (verified by direct curl + text extraction): "石油製品需給動態統計調査は、統計法に基づく基幹統計調査（基幹統計である石油製品需給動態統計を作成するための調査）として、石油製品の製造業者、輸入業者等を対象に、石油製品の需給の実態を明らかにすることを目的とする。" (Translation: The Petroleum Products Supply-Demand Statistics Survey is conducted as a fundamental statistics survey under the Statistics Act, to compile the fundamental statistics on petroleum product supply and demand.) This is the current successor/component of METI's petroleum statistics suite described by this node.

UPDATE 2026-08-29 (Grok follow-up, raw-verified by the orchestrating session via direct curl fetch of the official NRA PDF). NRA's own Convention on Nuclear Safety 10th National Report states the reactor-status categories rest on NRA's statutory reporting/oversight regime: "In the event of an accident or failure at a nuclear facility, a licensee is required to immediately report the incident to the NRA in accordance with the Reactor Regulation Act. The licensee is also obligated to promptly provide the NRA with a report detailing the situation and the measures taken in response to the event." And, on operational status: "In the event that a reactor facility deviates from its limiting conditions for operation, the licensee must immediately declare the deviation and report it to the NRA." The reactor-status categories (in operation, suspended, under construction, under decommissioning) that this node publishes are NRA's own regulatory classifications under this reporting regime.

UPDATE 2026-08-29 (Grok follow-up, raw-verified by the orchestrating session via direct curl fetch of the official NRA PDF; a supplementary TEPCO PDF Grok also cited returned HTTP 403 and was NOT used as evidence). NRA's own Convention on Nuclear Safety 10th National Report states: "TEPCO Fukushima Daiichi NPS was designated as a Specified Nuclear Facility by the NRA on 7 November 2012, in accordance with the Reactor Regulation Act. Subsequently, on 14 August 2013, TEPCO obtained NRA approval for ‘Implementation Plan for the Specified Nuclear Facilities at TEPCO Fukushima Daiichi NPS’ (Implementation Plan), under which special safety measures have been implemented." Decommissioning progress reporting operates under this NRA-approved Implementation Plan.

UPDATE 2026-08-29 (Grok follow-up, raw-verified by the orchestrating session via direct curl fetch of the official MIC PDF; Shift-JIS decoding needed to read the source page correctly). MIC's own follow-up report on the Basic Plan for the Development of Official Statistics states: "法第54条においては、総務大臣は、公的統計を利用しようとする者の便利を図るため、インターネットの利用を通じて迅速に公的統計の所在に関する情報を提供できるよう必要な措置を講ずるものとされている。" (Article 54 requires the Minister to operate a portal providing rapid access to official statistics info) "...「政府統計の総合窓口（e-Stat）」を運営している...e-Statは法第８条及び第23条の規定に基づく統計の公表の取組の中核を担っている" (e-Stat is central to the statistics-publication work required under Articles 8 and 23 of the Act). This is an official MIC document naming e-Stat's specific legal basis under the Statistics Act 2007.
